sources.note: No descriptive source: both references (Hudson 1994; Knappert 1905) are rated 'a wordlist or less'; Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology. Classification Barito-Mahakam after Hudson 1994 pp. 11, 20; Ethnologue status 'extinct'.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Ampanang language' (wikitext downloaded 2026-09-17) and Wikipedia (id) 'Bahasa Ampanang'.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. en: extinct, known only from Knappert's 19-word list (pp. 615-616), village of Ampanang on the Kahala river (Kenohan, Kutai Kartanegara); id: 'Bahasa Ampanang atau Bahasa Jambuk', Bongan district, Kutai Barat, 30,000 speakers after Wurm & Hattori 1981 (via Ethnologue).

sources.citation: Knappert, S. C. 1905. Beschrijving van de Onderafdeeling Koetei. Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde van Nederlandsch-Indië 58: 575-654 (DOI 10.1163/22134379-90001995). Ampanang material at pp. 590 and 615-616.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. It is a colonial administrative description of Kutai; the Ampanang content is one remark (p. 590) that the people of Ampanang speak 'een afzonderlijk dialect' and a 19-word Dutch-Ampanang list plus the autonym 'Behasa Ampanang' (pp. 615-616), in Dutch orthography (ĕ = schwa, é = close e; no stress marks), with the note that only the old still know it and the young mix it with Kutai and Malay. No phonological or prosodic statement of any kind.
